text:
sam: Kicking off a short RFC thread — we need a PRD + acceptance criteria for Private Deploy: customer-managed networking (VPC / on-prem). Goal: clear launch gates so sales/platform know what to promise. Quick takes?

maria: +1. Suggest we separate flows: 1) Cloud VPC peering, 2) Customer VPN to our private control plane, 3) Fully on-prem / air-gapped. Each requires different network prerequisites.

ian: Core technical requirements from runtime side: deterministic egress (customer controls outbound CIDRs), support for split-horizon DNS, NAT / SNAT mapping docs, and graceful failover for KV cache when route changes. Also document max MTU assumptions.

jules: Security checklist: customer-managed KMS integration or bring-your-own-key, audit log forwarding (syslog/S3), and validated TLS-termination options. Acceptance criteria: security signoff + threat-model reviewed. No PII should be logged in plaintext.

ashley: Ops/gating: rollout plan must include canary (10% traffic), synthetic smoke tests (latency, correctness), and an automated rollback if error rate >2% sustained for 5m. Define latency SLOs per class: short sequences p50 < 60ms, p95 < 250ms for Dedicated hardware baseline.

maria: Edge cases to call out: split-horizon DNS causing mixed-success responses, asymmetric routing breaking TLS session resumption, customer BGP flap scenarios that invalidate KV caches and cause cold starts. Propose mitigations: sticky session tokens, ephemeral cache warming request path.

ian: Minimal customer prerequisites section: required CIDR ranges to allow, preferred BGP config (optional), sample ACL entries. Quick sample snippet for firewall rules:```yaml
allowed_outbound:
  - cidr: 198.51.100.0/24    # control-plane egress
  - cidr: 203.0.113.0/24     # inference endpoints
ports:
  - 443
  - 5222  # health/probes
```

jules: Also require an emergency access plan: one-off timeboxed SSH tunnel or temporary provisioning path with customer signoff. Add compliance gating for SOC2 / ISO customers — require SOC2 cert present and a documented data flow.

ashley: Acceptance criteria draft (ops-friendly):
- End-to-end inference smoke: request -> response validated against golden prompts (pass rate >=98%)
- Network resilience: loss of path -> failover within 30s, no data corruption
- Observability: token-level cost/latency shown in Console for the private deployment route
- Security: KMS + audit log delivery confirmed in staging
- Runbook: documented rollback and emergency-contact list provided

sam: Prioritization / timeline: make this P0 for regulated pilot customers (legal/compliance will require). Suggested schedule: 6-week pilot (setup + 2 pilot customers) then 4-week GA hardening. If not pilot, treat as P1 and extend timeline.

maria: I'll draft the PRD sections: scope, non-goals, acceptance criteria, rollout plan, and checklist for customer handoff. Will link to a draft RFC in the repo by EOD.

deploy-bot: RFC created: https://redwood.internal/rfcs/priv-deploy-networks-1865432100 (draft) :robot_face:

sam: Action items: @maria draft PRD + checklist, @ian add detailed network diagrams and sample configs, @jules add security signoff checklist, @ashley write canary playbook. We'll reconvene in 48h. :thumbsup:

jules: One final ask — include explicit acceptance test for DNS misrouting (simulate split-horizon) and a test for partial egress blackhole. Those two have bitten us in past.

ashley: Noted. I'll add automated chaos test into the canary to simulate route flaps.

maria: Thanks everyone — I'll post the PRD link in this thread when ready.

sam: Thanks. Keeping this thread for PRD -> RFC comments.
